title: Airport in the Sky
label: adventure
story: Twenty-two miles of open water, then a runway on a mountaintop at 1,602 feet. Catalina rewards careful planning: altitude for glide range over the channel, and a hump in the middle of the runway that hides the far end.
objectives: Plan a crossing altitude that keeps you within gliding distance of land as long as practical
Brief the KAVX runway hump, cliffs and downdrafts on short final
Land at KAVX and get the famous buffalo burger

title: Class C Arrival
label: cfi_verified
story: Two-way radio contact, a squawk code and a landing among the airliners. Burbank or John Wayne turns busy airspace from intimidating into routine.
objectives: Get the ATIS and establish contact with approach before the Class C ring
Fly assigned headings and altitudes, and copy a landing clearance
Land at KBUR or KSNA

title: Coastal Cross-Country
label: potentially_qualifying
story: Up the coast past Point Mugu to Santa Barbara: more than 50 nm from home, with a marine layer to plan around and plenty of airspace to talk to.
objectives: Plan the route with checkpoints and fuel
Land at KSBA, more than 50 nm straight-line from your departure airport
Close your flight plan

title: Santa Paula
label: adventure
story: A one-runway airport full of vintage aircraft and a Sunday open house. A short, narrow runway between hills makes for a good precision landing.
objectives: Fly a stabilized approach to a short, narrow runway
Land at KSZP

title: LAX Special Flight Rules Area
label: adventure
story: Fly straight over the LAX runways on the Special Flight Rules Area route, with the published altitudes and self-announced position reports.
objectives: Study the SFRA procedures and altitudes on the terminal area chart
Self-announce on the SFRA frequency
Cross the SFRA box over LAX

title: High Country
label: cfi_verified
story: Mammoth Yosemite sits at 7,135 feet. Density altitude, mountain winds and terrain make this a flight to plan with an instructor first.
objectives: Compute takeoff and climb performance for the density altitude
Plan an escape route for mountain wave and downdrafts
Land at an airport above 7,000 ft
prerequisites: Performance planning reviewed by a CFI

title: Big Bear Density Altitude
label: adventure
story: At 6,752 feet and on a warm afternoon, Big Bear can feel like flying at 10,000. Lean for best power and watch the climb rate.
objectives: Lean for best power before takeoff
Land at L35

title: Palm Springs
label: adventure
story: Over the Banning Pass, where the wind can be strong and bumpy, into the desert. Plan for heat, turbulence and wind farms.
objectives: Brief the Banning Pass winds
Land at KPSP

title: Santa Ynez Wine Country
label: adventure
story: A quiet valley airport a short walk from tasting rooms. Coastal fog and the Gaviota Pass winds are part of the planning.
objectives: Plan around coastal fog
Land at KIZA

title: Owens Valley
label: adventure
story: Between the Sierra and the White Mountains, the deepest valley in the country. Smooth mornings, big afternoon winds.
objectives: Plan to arrive before the afternoon winds
Land at KBIH

title: Practice Diversion
label: cfi_verified
story: Your instructor picks a new destination mid-flight. Estimate heading, distance, time and fuel, and get there.
objectives: Divert to an alternate your CFI chooses
Estimate heading, time and fuel within a few minutes of flying it
prerequisites: Flown with a CFI, who verifies it

title: Three-Point Cross-Country
label: potentially_qualifying
story: The big one before the checkride: full-stop landings at three airports, one more than 50 nm from home, about 150 nm in all.
objectives: Full-stop landings at three airports, including your departure airport
One landing more than 50 nm straight-line from your departure airport
About 150 nm in total
prerequisites: Solo cross-country endorsement from your CFI
